name: Square screen and knob
look: a desk device with a square screen on the left and a chunky knob that clicks on a raised panel on the right
picture_prompt: Product concept render of a small 3D-printable desk device, seen from the front and slightly to one side. It is a little wider than it is tall. One smooth continuous body with soft rounded corners. On the left of the front is a flat square screen, about 28 mm across. On the right is a raised panel with one chunky round knob. One matte plastic colour with a dark screen. Soft studio light, plain light background. Flat bottom, flat back, no text, no logos, no speaker holes, no feet, no visible seams, no cables.
sheet: Front faces -y and stands upright. World +z is up.
Left about 60% of the front: the screen, a separate board with its long side along z, just behind the front wall.
Right part of the front: a raised control panel, stepping forward as far as the knob's plugs need, across the full height of the case, with a rounded transition.
The knob comes straight out of that panel toward -y. It is also the button: pressing it clicks. Its pins point -y too.
The controller is a separate board behind the screen, so its USB reaches the left wall. Its top faces the back (+y) and its pins point forward (-y), with their plugs between it and the screen.
USB opens on the left side (-x).
The wires run behind the screen board as one neat bundle, side by side, and do not show from outside.
The seam is a flat plane near the back, so from the front the Shell looks like one continuous body and the Base is only a rear cover.
The controller sits on a holder built into the rear cover. The rear cover is a flat plate with holder and stops on it, and it closes from +y.
